# [Baseline] - WIN - U - Microsoft Teams

Limits sign-in in Teams to the organisation's own tenant and prevents Teams from starting itself immediately after installation.

| | |
|---|---|
| Platform | Windows |
| Scope | User (U) — assign to user groups |
| Type | Settings Catalog |
| Assignment | — |
| checkId | `INTUNE-BASE-145-UMicrosoftTeams` |
| Source | IntuneAdmin/IntuneBaselines — Windows 11 Benchmarks/Microsoft Teams |
| File | [`Baseline_WIN_U_Microsoft_Teams.json`](Baseline_WIN_U_Microsoft_Teams.json) |

> The tenant id is set as `%OrganizationId%` in the template. On deployment, CIPP replaces it with the tenant's customerId (see Get-CIPPTextReplacement); `%tenantid%` does the same. The OneDrive policies already use the same construction for their tenant list. If you deploy with IntuneBackupAndRestore instead of CIPP, that replacement does not happen and you must fill in the id by hand. Separate multiple tenants with a comma. The second setting is convenience, not security: Teams does not start immediately after installation.
